t: This is the Curzon Mayfair Cinema at 37–38 Curzon Street, a Grade II listed building put up between 1963 and 1966. Horace Gael Hammond, known as H. G. Hammond, designed it for the architects Sir John Burnet, Tait and Partners. He lived from 1910 to 2006. Historic England describes it as the finest surviving cinema building of the post-war period, and also the least altered. So when you step inside, you're in a cinema that remains very close to how it was first built.
